title: Illustration / Characters / Body types
slide_intent: Build varied characters from simple pieces so their identity survives changes of scale and pose.
strategic_value: Different proportions within a shared geometric approach can let Duolingo represent a broad cast without losing consistency or making production unwieldy.
demonstration: Six translucent construction figures form two rows at left, varying the head, torso and limb proportions; explanatory copy sits at right.
practical_value: Choose a small number of basic head and body shapes, then vary proportions and features to distinguish the character.

content_islands.name: Body construction examples
content_islands.spec: Arrange six pale blue outlined figures in two rows of three at left, exposing overlapping head, torso and limb shapes.

content_islands.name: Construction rationale
content_islands.spec: Place the Body Types heading and explanation at right, connecting simplicity with scaling and posing while allowing customization.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text links simple pieces to scalability in both image size and production, and to easier posing.
reference_purposes.Expression: The six distinct silhouettes demonstrate variety within one geometric character language.
reference_purposes.Application: The examples offer multiple head and torso combinations.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The source says heads and bodies usually use 1–2 basic shapes each; it leaves widths, heights, shapes and facial features customizable.

ingredient.name: Simple character bodies
ingredient.role: Keep characters distinct while making them easy to scale and pose.
ingredient.application: Usually compose the head and body from 1–2 basic shapes each; customize proportions and facial features.
ingredient.scope: Historical official Duolingo illustration guidance from the 2024–2025 archived snapshot. The 1–2-shape statement is a usual construction pattern, not an absolute limit on every character.
